questions.stem: In triangle ABC, angle A = 40 degrees, angle B = 65 degrees, and side a = 8 cm (opposite angle A). Find side b to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: By the Sine Rule: b/sin(B) = a/sin(A). So b = 8 x sin(65)/sin(40) = 8 x 0.9063/0.6428 = 8 x 1.4098 = 11.3 cm (1 d.p.).

questions.stem: In triangle PQR, angle P = 50 degrees, side p = 12 cm (opposite P), and side q = 9 cm (opposite Q). Find angle Q to 1 decimal place.
In triangle ABC, angle A = 35 degrees, angle C = 80 degrees, and side c = 15 cm. Find side a to 1 decimal place.
When should you use the Sine Rule rather than the Cosine Rule?

options.text: When you know two sides and the included angle (SAS)
When you know all three sides (SSS)
When you know a matching pair of angle and opposite side (AAS or ASA)

questions.explanation: The Sine Rule requires a matching pair (an angle and its opposite side). Use it for AAS, ASA, or SSA situations. SAS and SSS require the Cosine Rule.
